newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says processing Busang contract of work.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says processing Busang contract of work.

text.p: Indonesia's director general of mining, Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, said on Tuesday the government was still processing contracts of work for two sections of the Busang gold find in East Kalimantan province.
"We are still processing (Busang II and III) but they have not yet been approved by President Suharto," Kuntoro told reporters. He did not know when they would be ready.
The Busang II section contains the bulk of the gold discovered so far on the property, estimated by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd to contain some 71 million ounces of gold.

Busang I, for which Bre-X and its Indonesian partners already have a contract of work, is estimated to contain about three million ounces of gold. Little exploration work has been done so far on Busang III.
Kuntoro said Suharto had approved 68 other contracts of work (COWs) not connected with Busang.
"It is correct that they have been approved by the president. We are still processing them (the 68 COWs). I hope the processing will be concluded this week," he said.
He said a date had still to be set for the signing of the COWs by the ministry and the companies involved.
The COWs are required for further exploration and development of mining claims.
Bre-X has 45 percent stake in Busang II and III, Indonesian interests 40 percent and the U.S. Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, which is to develop the property, 15 percent.

Bre-X shares were hit last Friday following the death of the company's chief geologist Michael de Guzman, who fell from a helicopter on his way to Busang last Wednesday, and an Indonesian newspaper report questioning the size and viability of the Busang find.
Kuntoro said he had no comment on the gold in Busang II and Busang III.
Bre-X shares partially rebounded on Monday after the company issued a statement saying it was confident that the assay results and estimates of gold reserves at Busang were accurate.
Freeport-McMoRan said last Friday it was still conducting a due diligence process at Busang, a highly detailed survey of the site.
